item.title: How Anthropic Redesigned Source Control for AI-Driven Development
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/anthropic-source-control/en/headerimage/scion-architecture-header-1792669549048.jpeg"/><p>Anthropic recently detailed how it migrated its monorepo from Git to Scion. Scion is a source control system that moves repository operations to the server side and uses content-addressed storage and tiered caches for agent and CI workloads. The design sacrifices offline independence for less local data and shared infrastructure.</p> <i>By Eran Stiller</i>

item.title: Presentation: Serving LLMs at Scale: The Hidden KV Cache Advantage
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/llm-inference-kv-cache/en/mediumimage/medium-1792066105733.jpeg"/><p>Khawaja Shams shares a distributed systems perspective on scaling LLM inference stacks efficiently. He discusses practical strategies for optimizing GPU utilization, managing KV cache memory cliffs, leveraging tiered storage, reducing tail latency, and implementing disaggregated prefill and decode architectures to improve overall fleet performance, cost economics, and availability.</p> <i>By Khawaja Shams</i>

item.title: AWS Shows Use of AI Agents to Triage Linux Kernel CVEs
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/aws-ai-agents-linux-kernel-cves/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793031817205.jpg"/><p>Engineers from Amazon Web Services (AWS) have described how the team that maintains the Linux kernel for EC2 infrastructure handles kernel CVEs. The process combines an automated filter, an AI agent and human review. The team also argues that it needs to move to newer long-term-support (LTS) kernels, as older branches collect fixes that are never backported.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

item.title: Cloudflare and VoidZero Introduce tsrs: An AI-Generated Rust Port of TypeScript
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-tsrs-ai-typescript/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793039825386.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare, VoidZero and Max Schwenk announced tsrs, an experimental Rust port of the TypeScript compiler, built with the TypeScript team's involvement. Cloudflare claims up to 8x faster checking and 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0, though one test against 7.1 beta showed 2.7x. It lacks watch mode and a language server, and exits with code 2 on type errors.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Developers Reporting Double-Digit Weekly Time Savings from AI Fell from 68% to 26%
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/atlassian-devex-2026/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793026389174.jpg"/><p>Atlassian’s State of Developer Experience 2026 finds the share of developers saving ten or more hours a week with AI dropped from 68% to 26% year over year, while only 28% report noticeably less friction than before AI. Engineering leaders report spending more time managing and correcting AI output than developers do.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: OpenTofu 1.13 Lets Module Authors Reduce Unknown Values at Plan Time
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/opentofu-1-13-unknown-values/en/headerimage/header-1792823798248.jpeg"/><p>OpenTofu 1.13 adds convert and assume... functions that let module authors give the planner type and value hints for unknown values, so more expressions resolve during tofu plan. If a value unknown during planning later violates a guarantee, OpenTofu reports an error during apply.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/digitalocean-self-improving-ai/en/headerimage/digitalocean-managed-agents-1793035926117.jpeg"/><p>DigitalOcean has announced the public preview of Learning Services and Agent Data Services, enabling developers to build, evaluate, and continuously improve AI agents within a unified, AI-native, cloud platform.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: Production AI and Engineering Team Design: InfoQ’s November Certification Cohorts
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/online-cohorts-nov-certification/en/headerimage/InfoQ-Nov-Cohorts-v3-1793013188536.jpg"/><p>A preview of three November InfoQ online certification cohorts covering production AI systems, retrieval and agent design, engineering team flow, AI roles, and measurement, facilitated by Adi Polak, Lan Chu, and Olimpiu Pop.</p> <i>By Artenisa Chatziou</i>

item.title: Java News Roundup: JDK 28 Schedule, Oracle CPUs, eMudhra Certs, Apache POI, WildFly, Azul, BellSoft
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/java-news-roundup-oct19-2026/en/headerimage/java-news-roundup-image-1793025199136.jpg"/><p>This week's Java roundup for October 19th, 2026, features news highlighting: the proposed release schedule for JDK 28; the eMudhra Intermediate CA certificates breach; the October 2026 Critical Patch Update; Azul and BellSoft CPUs; GA releases of WildFly 42 and Apache POI 6.0; the beta release of Open Liberty 26.0.0.11; and maintenance releases of Micronaut and JobRunr.</p> <i>By Michael Redlich</i>

item.title: Readyon Builds Four Layer Tenant Isolation for Multi Tenant Amazon EKS
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>ReadyOn has detailed a four-layer tenant isolation architecture for its Harmony platform on Amazon EKS. The design combines Kubernetes namespaces, dedicated Karpenter node pools, VPC security groups, and per-tenant Aurora databases, with controls evaluated against a 10-stage multi-tenant threat model focused on cross-tenant access and lateral movement.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: Article: The Evolution of Agentic Harnesses: From Chains to Graph to Code
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/agentic-ai-architecture-harness-evolution/en/headerimage/agentic-ai-architecture-harness-evolution-header-1792744961862.jpg"/><p>Agentic LLM systems have moved from linear prompt chains to graph-based workflows and, more recently, code-executing harnesses. Chains are simple but fragile, graphs add branching, retries, and validation, and code harnesses verify outputs through execution. The article advises validating model outputs and choosing the least complex design that meets reliability, speed, and cost needs.</p> <i>By Karthik Ramgopal</i>

item.title: Cloudflare’s Auto Router Rates Each Request for Stakes, from the Most Recent Turns
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-auto-router/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792492628413.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has released Auto Router in public beta through AI Gateway, picking a model per request from a classifier that scores complexity, ambiguity, stakes and context dependence. Cloudflare’s own benchmark puts it ten points below Claude Opus 5.5 on success rate at a third of the cost, and practitioners have questioned how stakes survive a long agent session.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: MCP C# SDK 2.0 Makes HTTP Stateless by Default and Adds Multi Round-Trip Requests
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/MCP-CSharp-SDK-Stateless/en/headerimage/header-1792707557585.jpg"/><p>Microsoft announced version 2.0 of the official MCP C# SDK, which implements the 2026-07-28 revision of the Model Context Protocol with stateless HTTP servers by default, standardised routing headers and Multi Round-Trip Requests. Releases 2.1 to 2.3 have since added hybrid session serving, a subscriptions/listen handler and a series of discovery, OAuth and shutdown fixes.</p> <i>By Edin Kapić</i>

item.title: PyTorch Conference 2026: Google and Meta Open-Source TorchTPU for Native PyTorch on TPUs
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/google-meta-torchtpu/en/headerimage/torchtpu-header-1792934272172.jpg"/><p>Google and Meta open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for Google's TPUs, at PyTorch Conference North America 2026, and Meta said it plans to move larger LLM workloads onto TPUs with it. AWS released TorchNeuron for Trainium the same week, while developers questioned TPU availability and where vendor lock-in now sits.</p> <i>By Andrew Hoblitzell</i>

item.title: Google’s Data Agent Kit Hits GA, Splitting Agent Guardrails Between Skills and IAM
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Google has made Data Agent Kit generally available, a free set of MCP tools and 37 open-source skills that connect coding agents to more than fifteen Google Data Cloud services. Two kinds of guardrail ship with it, and practitioners need to tell them apart: one is a skill asking the agent to stop, the other an IAM deny policy that refuses the call.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Cloudflare Reclaims 100 TB of RAM by Optimizing Consistent Hashing
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-hashing-optimization/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790410589563.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare recently documented how it reduced the memory footprint of its internal load-balancing service by more than 100 TB by optimizing the Rust implementation of consistent hashing in pingora-ketama. The changes compacted hash-ring entries and used statistical analysis of hash distribution and collision rates to reduce the number of hashes per backend by about 90%.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

item.title: Cloudflare Brings On-Demand CPU and Memory Profiling to Production Workers
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-cpu-memory-profiling/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791971960113.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has introduced on-demand CPU and memory profiling for Workers and Durable Objects, allowing developers to investigate performance bottlenecks in production using interactive flamegraphs.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: Article: Multi-Cloud FinOps: an Engineering Framework for Cross-Cloud Cost Optimization
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/multi-cloud-finops-cost-optimization/en/headerimage/multi-cloud-finops-cost-optimization-header-1792499448017.jpg"/><p>Multi-cloud flexibility comes with hidden egress costs driven by service placement and communication patterns. This article applies Backend FinOps to cross-cloud architecture, covering cost visibility through FOCUS, workload placement, synchronization models, and CI/CD-integrated cost governance. A controlled experiment shows architecture changes saved far more than rate negotiation alone.</p> <i>By Vivek Arora</i>

item.title: Presentation: Move Fast, Don’t Break Trust: Shipping Constantly with Humans and Beyond
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/monzo-microservices-devex/en/mediumimage/suhail-patel-medium-1791448951499.jpg"/><p>Suhail Patel discusses how Monzo structures its software engineering organization and technical stack to ship safely hundreds of times a day. He shares insights into opinionated microservice abstractions, tenancy-based staging, static analysis checks, continuous profiling, demonstrating how a strong internal platform enables engineers and LLMs to iterate rapidly without sacrificing reliability.</p> <i>By Suhail Patel</i>

item.title: NgRx 22: Resource Extensions and Dynamic Deep Signals for Angular
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/ngrx-22-angular/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792664456149.jpg"/><p>NgRx 22 adds experimental resource extensions that change Angular's resource behavior, so value() is retained during reloads and no longer throws on errors. It also introduces dynamic deep signals for union types, a SignalStoreFeatureType utility, and ESLint v10 support. Upgrading requires Angular 22 and TypeScript 6.0, and most breaking changes have automated migrations.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Harbor Adds Docker Sandboxes to Run Reproducible AI Agent Evals in Isolated MicroVMs
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/ai-agents-harbor-docker/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792589629439.jpg"/><p>Docker announced that Harbor, the open-source agent evaluation framework, now works with Docker Sandboxes. This change allows each evaluation task to run in its own microVM. So, instead of sharing a container, tasks are isolated for better performance</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

item.title: Developer behind the AI-Built Adobe Clones Says They Are “Not Anywhere Close to Ready"
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>A developer used Claude Opus 5.5 to build open-source replacements for seven Adobe applications, promoted them across Reddit with a projection of roughly 100% parity within a month, then told Hacker News the project was not anywhere close to ready. Its own roadmap puts it at 45% ready for real work and 2,300 to 4,100 agent-hours from full parity.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: NestJS 12: ESM Packages, Standard Schema Validation and Native Observability
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/nestjs-12-observability/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792168374584.jpg"/><p>NestJS version 12 has been released, transitioning core packages to ESM and adding Standard Schema validation. It updates the CLI and introduces an observability SDK. Key changes include project generation choices between CJS and ESM, improved validation options, and lifecycle project hooks. Users will need Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+. Migration guides are available for upgrading.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>
